provenance: Official Digital Asset RPC Infrastructure README, root LICENSE, workspace Cargo.toml, DAS API pagination validation, and related-asset DAO query inspected at commit 9c7e1b6bb97962acba17b62e522e18b9cb3abc4f
Checkout encountered Windows MAX_PATH errors for several long integration-fixture paths; inspected production README/API/DAO source files were present, but the checkout is not complete
discoveries: The repository describes a validator-message ingester, typed Postgres-backed Metaplex asset store, and JSON-RPC API for filtering/search and compressed-NFT Merkle proofs; it is an NFT/DAS index, not a fungible token market feed.

The inspected API validates mutually exclusive page/cursor/before/after modes, caps page limits at 1000, and only permits ID sorting with cursor pagination; related queries use the asset ID as a deterministic secondary sort key.

The root LICENSE is GNU AGPL-3.0; the workspace is version 0.7.2 with publish=false and depends on a validator-plugin/Redis/Postgres-oriented deployment. No SYLPH dependency or trading integration is appropriate without a separate license and architecture decision.
patterns: make pagination modes mutually exclusive and reject unsupported sort/cursor combinations
use a stable ID tie-breaker to keep page ordering deterministic
separate validator ingestion and derived query APIs while preserving canonical source provenance
sources.overlap: Potential reference for paginated derived-data research interfaces only; SYLPH's signal path uses fungible token and pool observations, while this service indexes Metaplex digital assets and proofs. No runtime overlap requiring an adapter was found.
risks: AGPL-3.0 requires legal review before code reuse or linking
NFT/DAS asset state is not fungible token liquidity, mint safety or executable quote evidence
the source checkout is incomplete on Windows because several fixture paths exceed path limits
validator plugin, Redis, Postgres and cluster deployment add infrastructure and an independent data trust boundary
validation: if using any API pattern, test stable pagination under concurrent inserts/deletes and reject invalid cursor/sort combinations
compare any asset metadata to canonical on-chain account/program evidence
resolve the checkout path-length issue before claiming repository-wide source review
perform license review before any code/dependency reuse

provenance: Official validator-plugin README, root LICENSE, workspace Cargo manifests and Redis messenger implementation inspected at commit 2615ce96bedaabb217e2e0f0dc875991f85507bf
README consumer retry configuration compared with plerkle_messenger/src/redis/redis_messenger.rs implementation at the pinned commit
discoveries: The Rust Geyser plugin sends filtered account/transaction/block/slot observations through a binary Plerkle serialization layer to a message bus; it is validator-side indexing infrastructure, not a public SYLPH client.

README describes configurable queue buffers, worker counts, selected confirmation level, and consumer retries. The Redis implementation, after times_delivered exceeds retries, places the entry in an ACK list and XACKs it; this removes it from the pending retry path rather than preserving an unresolved delivery for independent recovery. The stream entry may remain until trimming, so the precise finding is loss of consumer pending/retry visibility, not necessarily immediate XDEL.

The README's stated Solana minimum is 1.10.41+, but current plerkle Cargo pins agave-geyser-plugin-interface and solana-transaction-status 4.2.2. The docs are not a safe compatibility contract. Root license is AGPL-3.0.
patterns: never silently ACK permanently unprocessed messages after a retry threshold; quarantine them with durable unresolved status
make queue depth, send latency, consumer lag, retry-exhaustion and dead-letter counts visible
pin plugin and validator interfaces and verify docs against the lockfile before rollout
sources.overlap: The plugin's validator buffer and Redis consumer are a separate producer/transport architecture. SYLPH consumes public Yellowstone/WSS and has a local canonical ingress queue, journal, backpressure, replay and gap-certificate mechanisms; adopting the plugin would require operating a validator and AGPL stack and would not itself fix SYLPH's consumer throughput.
risks: AGPL-3.0 requires legal review before code reuse or linking
retry exhaustion can remove an unprocessed message from the consumer pending set
filtered account/transaction updates are not complete chain history
processed commitment can be reverted and is not finality
README minimum-version claims conflict with current pinned Agave interfaces
validation: for any queue/consumer design, fault-inject a worker that never ACKs and verify exhausted messages remain visible/recoverable rather than silently disappearing
measure producer queue age/bytes, delivery attempts, consumer lag and end-to-end projection commit latency
test reconnect and replay against an independent canonical source
verify validator/plugin version compatibility from exact pinned interfaces
review AGPL-3.0 obligations before any reuse
